emails.subject: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body:
Hi Fernhill team,

Phase two is signed off internally, so we are ready when you are. The board asked for two extra things compared with our last call: a pricing page with a yearly/monthly toggle, and a resources section we can fill ourselves without coming back to you every time.

Can we still start on the 3rd?

emails.subject: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body:
Hi Anna,

Both additions are fine at this stage — neither changes the template set, so the estimate from last week stands. The resources section will use the same article template as the case studies, so you can publish without us.

The 3rd still works. I will send the kickoff agenda on Monday.

raw_headers.value: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff

emails.subject: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body:
Thanks, that works. I have put the two new pages into the sitemap document — nothing else moved.

One question on the resources section: if we add a post, does it need a design pass or is the template enough?

raw_headers.value: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff

emails.subject: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body:
The template is enough. Title, standfirst, one image, and a rich-text body — if a post needs more than that we should talk, because that means the template is wrong rather than the post being special.

Send the three posts whenever they are ready and I will run them through it.

raw_headers.value: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff

emails.subject: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body: Perfect. I will collect the first three posts and send them over on Thursday, then we can see whether the template holds up with real content.

raw_headers.value: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff

emails.subject: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body: Noted on the font licence — it is our licence, cleared for web and print, and I will put that in the handover note with the invoice number it was bought under.

raw_headers.value: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff

emails.subject: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff
emails.body: One last thing before the kickoff: could you include a short handover note about who owns the font licence? Our legal team asked and I would rather have it in writing.

raw_headers.value: Re: Website refresh — phase two kickoff

emails.subject: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body:
Hi,

I have read v3 twice. Four notes, only one of which is a real disagreement.

1. The clear-space rule on the logo is now 1x the cap height — that is tighter than what we use on the building signage. 2. The secondary palette is missing the two greens. 3. Type scale: fine. 4. The photography section tells people to shoot in daylight, which is not possible for a third of what we do.

Full markup attached — the guidelines PDF with my comments in the margins.

emails.subject: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body:
Hi Ines,

Thank you — this is exactly the kind of reading we hoped for. Taking them in order: clear space goes back to 1.5x, we will match the signage rule rather than defend the PDF.

The greens are real, they are just labelled wrongly; I will fix the label instead of the palette.

On photography you are right that the rule is unusable as written — I will rewrite it as a preference with a fallback.

raw_headers.value: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes

emails.subject: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body: On the greens: they are in the swatch sheet but marked "digital only". If facilities is using them on signage then the label is wrong, not the colour.

raw_headers.value: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes

emails.subject: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body: The greens are "accent, screen only" in the swatch sheet, which is a labelling mistake on our side given facilities has been printing them for a year. v4 removes the restriction.

raw_headers.value: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes

emails.subject: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body: Daylight is the wrong instruction, agreed. Something like "prefer daylight; if unavailable, match the colour temperature of the existing set" would cover both cases.

raw_headers.value: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes

emails.subject: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body: Rewritten as you suggested, with one added sentence about not mixing a daylight set with a fluorescent set in the same document. v4 on its way.

raw_headers.value: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes

emails.subject: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes
emails.body: All four resolved as far as I am concerned. Send v4 and I will sign it off the same day.

raw_headers.value: Re: Brand guidelines v3 — four notes

emails.subject: Photo licensing for the case study
emails.body:
Hi,

We would like to publish the Duarte Interiors case study on our own site as well as yours. Does the photographer's licence cover that, or do we need a second one?

raw_headers.value: Photo licensing for the case study

emails.subject: Re: Photo licensing for the case study
emails.body:
Hi Sofia,

Short answer: no. The licence we bought covers the campaign and this case study, not publication by a third party — and your site counts as a third party here, even though it is your own interiors.

A second licence for web use is about £180 and takes a week. Alternatively we link to the study on our site and you quote two images, which is free.

raw_headers.value: Re: Photo licensing for the case study

emails.subject: Re: Photo licensing for the case study
emails.body: Useful to know. The shoot was commissioned for the campaign, so I assumed web use everywhere was included.

raw_headers.value: Re: Photo licensing for the case study

emails.subject: Re: Photo licensing for the case study
emails.body: It is worth checking rather than assuming — the commission covered a specific set of placements. I have asked the photographer for a quote for the wider web licence so you have the number rather than my guess.

raw_headers.value: Re: Photo licensing for the case study

emails.subject: Re: Photo licensing for the case study
emails.body: Understood — two separate licences then. Could you send the wording you use for the credit line?

raw_headers.value: Re: Photo licensing for the case study

emails.subject: Contract draft — redlines attached

emails.subject: Re: Contract draft — redlines attached
emails.body: Two years is acceptable if it covers the case study as well as the portfolio. Redlined draft attached so you have the exact wording.

emails.subject: Re: Contract draft — redlines attached

Three of your seven unread messages look time-sensitive:

2. Marc Devereux - "Northgate audit timeline" moves the audit to the 22nd and asks whether anything would fail WCAG AA. That one needs an answer today; the staging fixes are already done, so it is a short reply.

"Hi Marc,

The 22nd works for us. Two things we already know about: the focus ring on the dark header is too low contrast, and the carousel does not pause on hover. Neither is structural, and both are already fixed in staging.

That leaves a week of margin before the audit.

Best,
Fernhill Studio"
